root_cause.text: The nci_transceive() function assumes ownership of the skb parameter but fails to free it on three early error return paths (-EPROTO, -EINVAL, and -EBUSY), causing memory leaks when these error conditions are encountered.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds kfree_skb(skb) calls before each of the three error returns in nci_transceive():

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix memory leaks in nci_transceive by freeing skb on all error return paths.
intent_record.what: Added three `kfree_skb(skb)` calls before early returns in the nci_transceive function at error paths: (1) when conn_info is NULL, (2) when target is not active, and (3) when NCI_DATA_EXCHANGE flag is already set. Also added braces around single-statement if blocks for consistency.
intent_record.how: This change prevents memory leaks by ensuring the skb (socket buffer) is freed before returning from error conditions. Previously, when these error paths were taken, the skb allocated at function entry would not be freed, causing memory to leak. Now all exit paths properly deallocate the skb.

grouping_result.intent: Fix memory leaks in nci_transceive by freeing skb on all error return paths.

bic_trace_step.reason: The nci_transceive() function in this commit adds an early error return at lines 730-731: 'if (!conn_info) return -EPROTO;' without freeing the skb parameter that was passed in. The function also has two other early returns at lines 742 (return -EBUSY) and implicitly through nci_send_data() error handling that could leak the skb. The vulnerability root cause states that the function assumes ownership of skb but fails to free it on three early error paths (-EPROTO, -EINVAL, and -EBUSY). This commit introduces the -EPROTO return path without proper skb cleanup, and the existing -EBUSY path (line 742) also lacks skb_kfree() before returning. The fix would require adding 'kfree_skb(skb);' before each early return statement, but no such cleanup is present in this code.
